neighbours.label: Punctuation or a preposition that ends a clause and continues a hypothetical or past description ('spelled to her [in] her program', 'in a space suit [–] you can't open a window', 'go up to the reader[,] and push a button')
fire: The child had a deaf teacher, who must have fingerspelled to her in her intervention program.
Imagine you were up in a space station or outside in a space suit – you can't just open a window.
I would go up to the reader, and push a button on the cell phone to unlock it.
Most normal people would not be able to pass an Olympic-level drug test.
The club will keep up its interest in robotics and enter some tournaments, he said.
By now the boy's small allowance has probably ceased. The little he earned in May is gone.
If you were stuck on a ship at sea – you would have to ration the water carefully.
She would walk to the gate, and wave to the driver before the bus pulled away.
quiet: The child had a kind teacher, who often read stories to her at the end of the school day.
The station orbits the Earth every ninety minutes and holds six astronauts at a time.
The reader is mounted on the wall by the door and shows a green light when it is ready.
Most people enjoy a long walk on a warm evening and a cold drink on the porch afterwards.
The club meets every Thursday and works on its robots in the school library.
The boy's small allowance is paid on Fridays, and he usually saves half of it.
The ship sails from the harbour at dawn and arrives at the island by early evening.
The bus stops at the gate, and the driver opens the door for the children each morning.

notes: Heterogeneous top examples (commas, dashes, 'in', 'test'); expected to fail.
